items.title: Pay import charges for held parcel (unverified, possible scam)
items.computation: Calendar date printed in the letter: 09.11.2026 (a Monday), used as written. No period to count.

warnings: Likely a scam (fake customs/parcel notice): do not pay before verifying with the real carrier or German customs (Zoll). Genuine import VAT is normally collected by the carrier or Zoll, not by an unknown company.
The payee is 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.', which does not match the sender 'Paketzentrum Musterstadt'. Payee and sender names differ.
The letter sets a very short deadline (a few days) and threatens return or destruction of the parcel, which is a pressure tactic.
Contact is only via WhatsApp and a mobile number, and the email uses a generic 'clearance-mail.example' domain. Genuine customs offices do not do this.
The letter has no addressed sender details that can be verified, and it does not name the carrier or the sender of the parcel. Check whether you are actually expecting a parcel from outside the EU.

Today's date differs between the context messages (2026-11-07 and 2026-09-30). I used 2026-11-07 as instructed, so the 09.11.2026 deadline is 2 days away. Under the other date it would be further off.
